name: device-types
description:
Device42's raw `type` used to be handed straight to deviceType. Its values are physical / virtual / blade / cluster / other / unknown, which say how a device is REALIZED, not what kind of device it is -- and none of them is a runZero device type. The platform does not reject an unknown value: IdentifyTypeFromCustomIntegration tries its exact-match list, then normalize.DeviceType(), which title-cases whatever it does not recognise and returns it. It does not recognise "physical" or "virtual", so those became device types in their own right -- displacing the type runZero would otherwise fingerprint from hw_model and manufacturer, and making a type search over these assets useless.

9201 (type=physical) and 9202 (type=virtual) must therefore carry NO deviceType at all, which is what this scenario mainly locks. 9203 is a cluster, equally unmapped -- a Device42 cluster is a logical grouping and not a device.

What IS mapped stays inside the exact-match list. 9204's blade is a blade SERVER in Device42's vocabulary and becomes Server. 9205 shows the more specific field winning: device_sub_type spells a runZero type exactly ("Switch"), so it is honoured even though `type` beside it is the unmappable "physical".

All three raw fields survive as custom attributes rather than being dropped with the mapping -- they used to be in exclude_keys precisely because deviceType consumed them, and losing them along with the bad type would have been a second defect.

namespaced_ids is skipped as in the other device42 scenarios: the id is the bare Device42 id with no appliance scope.
